name: North-Western Catalan

allophone_rules.notes: Word-final cluster simplification (Wheeler 2005 §10.4; Recasens 1993; Veny 1982 ch. 3): an ABSOLUTELY word-final stop is DELETED after a homorganic nasal or lateral — camp [ˈkam], sang [ˈsaŋ], quant [ˈkwan], molt [ˈmol]. An innovation of CENTRAL, NORTH-WESTERN and NORTHERN Catalan against the Old-Catalan core, which keeps the stop; VALENCIAN and BALEARIC keep it too (camp [ˈkamp], molt [ˈmolt]), and the 4catac expert transcriptions confirm the split on the one token that is diagnostic because a vowel follows — molt alta = Central/North-Western [ˈmol ˈalt-] vs Valencian/Balearic [ˈmolt ˈalt-]. The isogloss is therefore Central + North-Western (+ Northern) against Valencian + Balearic; it is NOT the Eastern/Western line. Overrides the core's conservative CA_CLUSTER_*_FINAL rule by id.

Word-final cluster simplification (Wheeler 2005 §10.4; Recasens 1993; Veny 1982 ch. 3): an ABSOLUTELY word-final stop is DELETED after a homorganic nasal or lateral — camp [ˈkam], sang [ˈsaŋ], quant [ˈkwan], molt [ˈmol]. An innovation of CENTRAL, NORTH-WESTERN and NORTHERN Catalan against the Old-Catalan core, which keeps the stop; VALENCIAN and BALEARIC keep it too (camp [ˈkamp], molt [ˈmolt]), and the 4catac expert transcriptions confirm the split on the one token that is diagnostic because a vowel follows — molt alta = Central/North-Western [ˈmol ˈalt-] vs Valencian/Balearic [ˈmolt ˈalt-]. The isogloss is therefore Central + North-Western (+ Northern) against Valencian + Balearic; it is NOT the Eastern/Western line. Overrides the core's conservative CA_CLUSTER_*_FINAL rule by id.

Word-final cluster simplification (Wheeler 2005 §10.4; Recasens 1993; Veny 1982 ch. 3): an ABSOLUTELY word-final stop is DELETED after a homorganic nasal or lateral — camp [ˈkam], sang [ˈsaŋ], quant [ˈkwan], molt [ˈmol]. An innovation of CENTRAL, NORTH-WESTERN and NORTHERN Catalan against the Old-Catalan core, which keeps the stop; VALENCIAN and BALEARIC keep it too (camp [ˈkamp], molt [ˈmolt]), and the 4catac expert transcriptions confirm the split on the one token that is diagnostic because a vowel follows — molt alta = Central/North-Western [ˈmol ˈalt-] vs Valencian/Balearic [ˈmolt ˈalt-]. The isogloss is therefore Central + North-Western (+ Northern) against Valencian + Balearic; it is NOT the Eastern/Western line. Overrides the core's conservative CA_CLUSTER_*_FINAL rule by id.

The lleidatà hallmark opens word-final unstressed ⟨-a⟩ to [ɛ] (porta [ˈpɔɾtɛ], dia [ˈðiɛ]), which the positional rule applies to every word-final ⟨a⟩. But a STRESSED final ⟨-a⟩ — a monosyllable like pa [ˈpa], va [ˈba], or an oxytone — does not lower: the opening is a property of the reduced, unstressed final vowel only (Recasens 1996; Veny 1982 ch. 3). This rule restores [a] on a stressed word-final ⟨a⟩ that the positional rule over-lowered (the ca-x-occidental-010 arbitration: pa stays [ˈpa], engine over-lowered to [ˈpɛ]). The ``grapheme`` gate is what keeps this rule to its stated job: without it the rule matched ANY word-final stressed [ɛ] and so rewrote the ⟨è⟩ words too — cafè [kaˈfɛ] came out [kaˈfa], bè [ˈbɛ] as [ˈba], and the same for què, perquè, cinquè. A written ⟨è⟩ states the aperture of its own vowel (IEC 2016 ch. 3; Wheeler 2005 §3.1) and is never the reduced final ⟨-a⟩ this rule is about, so the source grapheme is the condition the rule always needed.

North-Western carries open-mid [ɔ] in these lexemes where the Western default would give close [o] (corre [ˈkɔɾe], vora [ˈβɔɾɛ], dona [ˈdɔnɛ]); Catalan spelling does not mark the contrast, so the open-[ɔ] words are listed (Recasens 1996; Veny 1982; the ca-x-occidental-009/010 arbitration). Pins ONLY the stressed vowel and lets final-⟨a⟩ opening and betacism run on.

NORTH-WESTERN lowering of the initial atonic ⟨e-⟩ to [a] before an IMPLOSIVE nasal or /s/ (Veny 1982 ch. 3, the nord-occidental section: «en síl·laba inicial àtona, e > a davant de nasal o de s implosiva»). estar [asˈta], estendre [asˈtendɾe], escales [asˈkales], encara [aŋˈkaɾa], enciam [anˈsjam], enrere [anˈreɾe].
SCOPE — nord-occidental ONLY, deliberately narrower than the measurement supports. The 4catac Valencian gold attests exactly the same change (17 of 18 eligible types), and an earlier revision of this wave declared the rule on ca-x-valencia too on the strength of a claimed Recasens 1996 §5; that section pointer could not be verified against the source, and gold agreement is not a justification. Until a Valencian-scoped citation is in hand the rule stays on the variety Veny names.
THREE gates, each load-bearing and each with a counter-case in the same neighbourhood:
1. WORD-INITIAL — the change is an initial-syllable one; a word-internal atonic ⟨e⟩ is untouched (temperatura, president).
2. UNSTRESSED — a stressed initial ⟨e⟩ stays [e], which is exactly what keeps the demonstratives and their paradigm out without listing them: este [ˈeste], esta [ˈesta], estos [ˈestos], estes [ˈestes].
3. THE NASAL / /s/ MUST BE IMPLOSIVE — followed_by_2 requires a further consonant, so the trigger is a coda. enorme [eˈnoɾme] keeps [e] because its /n/ is the onset of the next syllable, not a coda; likewise exercicis [eɡzeɾˈsisiz], where ⟨x⟩ is neither.
EASTERN Catalan does NOT have this change — ca, ca-x-balear and ca-x-nord reduce the same vowel to [ə] (escales [əsˈkaləs]) — so the rule is never declared on the shared ca-x-medieval ancestor.

WESTERN override of the inherited pan-Catalan CA_NASAL_PALATAL (same id, so it REPLACES the ca-x-medieval rule rather than adding to it): /n/ assimilates to a following palato-alveolar FRICATIVE or to the palatal lateral — enxampar-hi [aɲ ˈʃ...], any llunyà [ˈaɲ ʎuˈɲa] — but NOT to the AFFRICATES [tʃ dʒ]. Nasal place assimilation copies the place of the following consonant's CLOSURE (Recasens 1993 on Catalan nasal assimilation; Wheeler 2005 §10.3), and the closure phase of Catalan /tʃ dʒ/ is alveolar/dental, not palatal — so the nasal stays alveolar. This matters in Western Catalan specifically, because Western is the branch that realises ⟨j⟩/⟨g+e,i⟩ as the affricate [dʒ] where Eastern has the plain fricative [ʒ]: mengen [ˈmendʒen], enxampar [antʃamˈpa], un jutge [un ˈdʒudʒe]. The Eastern specs keep the inherited rule unchanged, where the same words have a fricative and DO palatalise the nasal (àngel [ˈaɲʒəl]).

stress.notes: Catalan accentuation per the Institut d'Estudis Catalans (IEC) norm (Gramàtica de la llengua catalana, ch. 3; Wheeler 2005 §3.1). A written accent (à è é í ò ó ú) always wins and marks the stressed vowel. Unmarked words are OXYTONE when they end in a consonant other than -s-preceded-by-a-vowel and other than -en/-in — including the consonant+s plurals (-ns, -rs, -ts, -nts, -ps …), which are oxytone because the plural preserves the stress of the singular (important → importants). A word ending in a falling DIPHTHONG (-ai -au -ei -eu -iu -oi -ou) is oxytone (remei [rəˈmɛj], correu [kuˈrɛw], avui [əˈβuj]) — the diphthong is one syllable, so the word does not end in a bare vowel. Unmarked words are PAROXYTONE when they end in a (single) vowel, in a vowel + -s (-as, -es, -is, -os, -us) or in -en/-in (semblen, parlin). The diaeresis ⟨ï ü⟩ marks hiatus/pronounced ⟨u⟩, NOT stress, so it is deliberately absent from marked_vowels (següent is [səˈɣwen], not [səˈɣwent] with stress on ⟨ü⟩). Proparoxytones always carry a written accent, so the unmarked default is paroxytone. The diphthongs list is the Catalan inventory of tautosyllabic vowel sequences (Wheeler 2005 §2.5; IEC grammar ch. 4): the falling diphthongs ⟨ai au ei eu iu oi ou ui⟩ and the rising ⟨ua ue uo ui⟩ after ⟨g/q⟩. Every other vowel sequence is HIATUS and counts as two syllables — te-ni-a, ve-ï-na, di-a — which is what puts the stress, and therefore the unstressed-vowel reduction, on the right vowel.

notes: NORTH-WESTERN CATALAN (català nord-occidental: lleidatà, pallarès, ribagorçà, tortosí), the northern half of the WESTERN block. It descends from Old Catalan (ca-x-medieval), not from Central Catalan. Kept from the core and therefore inherited: NO unstressed vowel reduction to [ə] (the seven-vowel system is maintained unstressed, que [ke], de [ðe] — Recasens 1996; Veny 1982 ch. 3), the affricate [dʒ] for ⟨j⟩/⟨g+e,i⟩ (juny [ˈdʒuɲ]) and the glide of ⟨ix⟩ = [jʃ] (caixa [ˈkajʃa]). Declared here: (1) its own hallmark, word-final unstressed ⟨-a⟩ opening to [ɛ] (una porta [ˈunɛ ˈpɔɾtɛ], dia [ˈðiɛ]) — the lleidatà final ⟨-a⟩, distinct from both the Central [ə] and the Valencian [a]; (2) ⟨x⟩ = [tʃ] word-initially and after a consonant (xiquet [tʃiˈket]), the Western affricate; (3) betacism, ⟨v⟩ merged into /b/, converging with Central; (4) deletion of word-final ⟨-r⟩ (aixecar [ajʃeˈka]); and (5) deletion of an absolutely word-final stop in an ⟨-nt/-lt/-mp/-nc⟩ cluster — North-Western simplifies after a LATERAL as well as after a nasal, exactly as Central does (molt [ˈmol]), which the 4catac expert transcriptions confirm (molt alta = [ˈmol ˈaltɛ], against Valencian and Balearic [ˈmolt ˈalta]). Points (3)–(5) are convergences with Central, not inheritances from it.

sources.author: Veny, J.

sources.notes: The standard dialectology of Catalan and the source for the isoglosses this spec encodes per dialect: final ⟨-r⟩ retained in Valencian and deleted in the rest; final-cluster simplification after a nasal everywhere but after a lateral only in the Eastern block; Western [tʃ] for initial ⟨x⟩ and [jʃ] for ⟨ix⟩; the lleidatà final ⟨-a⟩ = [ɛ]. Pages not verified.

sources.author: Institut d'Estudis Catalans
sources.title: Gramàtica de la llengua catalana
sources.notes: The normative grammar. Ch. 3 (l'accent) is the source for the stress block: the written accent marks the stressed vowel and always wins; unmarked words ending in a vowel, a vowel+⟨-s⟩ or ⟨-en/-in⟩ are paroxytone and all other endings — including the consonant+⟨s⟩ plurals — are oxytone; the diaeresis ⟨ï ü⟩ marks hiatus, not stress. §6.2 and the 'mots àtons' list are the source for the clitic function words (articles, contractions, atonic prepositions/conjunctions and weak pronouns) that carry no stress and therefore reduce. Cited by chapter; pages not verified.

Catalan spelling does not mark the ⟨e⟩/⟨o⟩ close/open contrast in unaccented syllables, so this contrast is lexical and can only be listed, not derived. Cited by headword; the dictionary is not paginated online.

sandhi_rules.name: atonic-article-vowel-elision-after-vowel-els
sandhi_rules.notes: Plural counterpart of CA_ELIDE_EL; see that rule's note for the phenomenon and its sources.

sandhi_rules.name: atonic-article-vowel-elision-after-vowel-el
sandhi_rules.notes:
ELISION OF THE ATONIC VOWEL of the proclitic masculine article / accusative clitic ⟨el⟩ ⟨els⟩ after a vowel-final word (Wheeler 2005 §11.2 'elision' and ch. 4 on the article's allomorphs; Bonet & Lloret 1998 ch. 5 on clitic vowel deletion; IEC 2016 §6.2 lists ⟨el/els⟩ among the atonic monosyllables). The article has no vowel of its own to defend: written ⟨l'⟩ before a vowel-initial word is the same allomorph, and after a vowel the support vowel is equally unnecessary — que el tap [ke l ˈtab], ningú el veu [niŋˈɡu l ˈβɛw], i el rei [i l ˈrej], voleu que els hòmens [ke lz ˈɔmens]. CLOSED CLASS by construction: the right context is the WHOLE word anchored at both ends, so only the two-segment clitic itself matches and no lexical word beginning in the same segments is touched (el·la, elefant, elzevir keep their vowel). The left context is a vowel: after a consonant the vowel is the only thing making the clitic pronounceable and it stays (amb el tap, per els). The engine already blocks every sandhi rule across a pause, so the elision cannot reach over an intonational-phrase boundary.
RELATION TO THE MINIMAL-WORD GUARD. The pan-Catalan hiatus rules (CA_ELIDE_INITIAL_VOWEL and the final-schwa rule) refuse to strip a word to nothing, and tests/test_catalan_phonology.py pins that. This rule is the ONE licensed exception and it is not a hiatus rule: it is closed-class, anchored on the whole word, and the licence is that Catalan ORTHOGRAPHY itself writes this article without a vowel — ⟨l'⟩ is the same article, not a different one (Wheeler 2005 ch. 4) — and the resulting proclitic attaches to the following word rather than standing alone. Every other monovocalic function word keeps its nucleus in these specs: estava en oració [asˈtaβa en oɾasiˈo].

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-sibilant-degemination-s
sandhi_rules.notes:
External (cross-word) SIBILANT DEGEMINATION: where a word ends in the same sibilant that the next word begins with, the phonological phrase has a single sibilant, not a geminate — the coda one is deleted (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.4 'consonant deletion in external sandhi'; Recasens 1993 §5). més són → [ˈme ˈson], dos savis → [ˈdo ˈsaβis], les sabates → [lə səˈβatəs], és seca → [ˈe ˈsɛkə].
Declared per DIALECT, not on the ca-x-medieval ancestor, because it is NOT pan-Catalan: Balearic assimilates and geminates instead of deleting, so ca-x-balear must not inherit this (see the note on ca-x-balear.json).
Scope, deliberately narrow on three axes, all measured. (1) IDENTICAL sibilants only: before a sibilant that DIFFERS in place or voicing the coda sibilant voices instead of deleting — petits juguen → [pəˈtidz ˈʒuɣən] (Wheeler 2005 §5.3), which CA_FINAL_TS_VOICING already handles. (2) SIBILANTS only: a cross-word stop or nasal geminate stays long in Catalan (tot tancat, constantment [kunstamˈmen]) and extending the deletion to stops or nasals measurably worsens every Catalan 4catac row. (3) VOICELESS sibilants only: word-final devoicing means no word surfaces with a final [z] or [ʒ] when these contexts are matched, so a z$ or ʒ$ rule could never fire. The consequence is that a /s # z/ boundary is currently left as a cross-word geminate (dos zeros → [ˈdoz ˈzɛɾus]) by CA_FINAL_S_VOICING: OUT OF SCOPE here, because collapsing it needs the deletion rules to see the post-voicing form, which the sandhi engine matches contexts against the ORIGINAL words to avoid. Pinned in tests/test_catalan_phonology.py::test_voiced_sibilant_boundary_is_a_known_gap.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-elision-initial-unstressed-vowel
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary, half two — ELISION of the next word's initial UNSTRESSED vowel. Where the left word does not end in the elidable [ə], the hiatus is resolved on the other side (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.).
Engine output, verified: va anar → [ˈba ˈna] (the 4catac gold writes the phrase as one word, [baˈna]; this library keeps the word boundary and the two forms are identical segment for segment), va experimentar → [ˈba kspəɾiməˈnta], he autoritzat → [ˈɛ wtuɾiˈdzat].
The two halves are mutually exclusive BY CONSTRUCTION, not by engine precedence: this rule's left context is the vowel set MINUS [ə], so a boundary whose left word ends in [ə] belongs to CA_ELIDE_FINAL_SCHWA and this rule cannot also fire on it. Exactly one vowel is lost per boundary.
High vowels are excluded from the right context for the same reason they are excluded from CA_ELIDE_FINAL_SCHWA's: an unstressed initial [i]/[u] GLIDES rather than deleting (CA_HIATUS_GLIDE_I / _U). Deletion and gliding partition the vowel space instead of competing for the boundary.
MINIMAL WORD. The context also guarantees the process cannot leave a word without a syllable: hiatus resolution in Catalan loses a vowel, never a word (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels. on clitic vowels and minimal-word behaviour). The lookahead requires ANOTHER vowel later in the same word, so a monovocalic word is never hollowed out: estava en oració keeps its preposition ([eˈstava en oɾasiˈo], not *[… n …]), que el keeps its article, and va a casa keeps its preposition [ˈba ə ˈkazə].
STRESS, and what the condition really does. An IPA stress mark precedes its vowel, so the unanchored right context ^[vowel] can only match a vowel with no mark on it. That is NOT the same as 'unstressed' in the prosodic sense: this engine writes no stress mark on an atonic monosyllable, so a clitic counts as unstressed here, which is right, while a stressed monosyllable that the engine leaves unmarked would also match. The condition is therefore 'carries no stress mark', and paga una is [ˈpaɣə wnə] rather than the gold's [ˈpaɣ ˈunə] precisely because the engine leaves una unmarked and the glide rule takes the boundary first.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-hiatus-glide-i
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary, the OTHER resolution — GLIDE FORMATION. A high vowel in hiatus need not delete: it loses its syllabicity and resyllabifies as an onset (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.). A word-initial unstressed [i] after a vowel-final word surfaces as [j] — engine output, verified: pollastre i → [puˈʎastɾə j], de dellà i tanca → [də ðəˈʎa j ˈtaŋkə]. Note the preceding [ə] is KEPT, which is why CA_ELIDE_FINAL_SCHWA excludes unstressed high vowels from its right context.
No minimal-word guard here, deliberately, and this is the ONE place the constraint is relaxed: the bare conjunction ⟨i⟩ is exactly the word this rule is for, and all four 4catac accents write it as [j] between vowels (pollastre i, i ara). Gliding does not delete a segment — it changes its syllabicity — so the word is still pronounced; requiring it to keep a nucleus would contradict the expert gold and measurably worsens the Valencian and North-Western rows.

sandhi_rules.name: cross-word-hiatus-glide-u
sandhi_rules.notes:
VOWEL CONTACT across a word boundary — GLIDE FORMATION, the [u] half of CA_HIATUS_GLIDE_I. A word-initial unstressed [u] after a vowel-final word surfaces as [w] — engine output, verified: beure un → [ˈbɛwɾə wn], sobte un → [ˈsoptə wn] (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels.).
MINIMAL WORD. The context also guarantees the process cannot leave a word without a syllable: hiatus resolution in Catalan loses a vowel, never a word (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.1 'vowel contact'; Bonet & Lloret 1998, *Fonologia catalana*, ch. 5 on hiatus resolution and clitic vowels. on clitic vowels and minimal-word behaviour). The lookahead requires a following segment, so a word that is nothing but [u] keeps its syllable: the conjunction ⟨o⟩, which the Eastern reduction realises as [u], stays syllabic in O Anna o Eva → [u ˈannə u ˈɛβə] instead of collapsing to a bare [w]. ⟨un⟩ has a consonant after the vowel and still glides, as the gold has it.
The MIRROR process on the LEFT side of the boundary — a word-final unstressed [i]/[u] gliding before a vowel-initial word (trobo adjectius [ˈtɾoβw ədʒəkˈtiws], deixo amor [ˈdeʃw əˈmor]) — is deliberately NOT declared: the Western accents write it with a non-syllabic diacritic on the original vowel quality ([ˈtɾoβo̯], [ˈðejʃo̯]) rather than as a plain glide, so one rule cannot state it for all four, and declaring the Eastern form measurably worsens the Valencian and North-Western rows.

sandhi_rules.name: monosyllabic-clitic-i-glides-before-vowel
sandhi_rules.notes:
A monosyllabic clitic whose whole form is [i] — the conjunction ⟨i⟩ and the adverbial pronoun ⟨hi⟩ — is syllabified into the following word as the glide [j] when that word begins with a vowel: hi havia [j əˈβiə], hi ha [j ˈa], i arribo [j əˈriβu], i ara [j ˈaɾə]. Wheeler 2005 ch. 12 (the syllabification of pronominal clitics) and ch. 11 (phrasal vowel sandhi); Bonet & Lloret 1998 ch. 5. The trigger is the FOLLOWING vowel, not a preceding one — which is what distinguishes this rule from the inherited CA_HIATUS_GLIDE_I, whose left context requires a preceding vowel and which therefore misses on hi ha, príncep i el and utterance-initial I arribo. ⟨i⟩ and ⟨hi⟩ are members of the spec's ``cliticless_words`` closed class (IEC 2016 §6.2). Confirmed in ALL FOUR 4catac dialect transcriptions (Central, Balearic, North-Western, Valencian), so it is declared on every dialect spec rather than on Central alone.
WESTERN NARROWING (this spec only): the right context excludes the clitic ⟨el⟩/⟨els⟩. There is nothing to glide into there — CA_ELIDE_EL removes that word's vowel at the very same boundary — and the sandhi engine resolves the two sides of a boundary INDEPENDENTLY, against the original words, so without the exclusion both rules fire and i el rei comes out as *[j l ˈrej]: two words, no syllable nucleus between them. With it the phrase is [i l ˈrej], which is how the 4catac North-Western gold writes it — the ⟨i⟩ keeps its nucleus and the article loses its own (Wheeler 2005 ch. 4 and §11.2; Bonet & Lloret 1998 ch. 5). Before any other vowel-initial word the clitic glides exactly as before: i ara [j ˈaɾa], i això.

sandhi_rules.name: external-nasal-palatalisation-western
sandhi_rules.notes: WESTERN override of the inherited CA_EXT_NASAL_PALATAL (same id, so it REPLACES it): the cross-word counterpart of this spec's CA_NASAL_PALATAL override — see that rule for the phenomenon and its sources. A word-final /n/ palatalises before a following palato-alveolar FRICATIVE or palatal lateral, but not before the affricates [tʃ dʒ], whose closure is alveolar: un jutge [un ˈdʒudʒe] in Western, against Eastern [uɲ ˈʒudʒə] where the same word begins with a fricative.
